findings.reason: The protected design is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. It stores each log once, gives the six timestamp precisions explicit names and lengths, and expresses retrieval as one readable inclusive scan. Its naturally produced insertion order is permitted but not promised. No candidate would materially improve correctness, asymptotic complexity, clarity, or structure.

Every timestamp field is zero-padded and ordered from year through second. Equal-length prefix comparison therefore matches chronological comparison at the selected precision. Truncating the stored timestamp and both query boundaries includes all entries in both endpoint buckets and every intervening bucket. The scan returns every matching unique ID, retains duplicate timestamps, survives repeated retrievals unchanged, and returns an empty list when no log qualifies.

Authenticated Premium source hash be5ed377fd28d7363b4b8bb3669f2689b2e21fff161d070e66cc200a62ca1c9a and repository metadata agree on the unique-ID log model, fixed timestamp format, constructor, put, inclusive retrieve operation, six granularities, numeric field limits, and 500-call cap. The statement does not require result order, and verified submission 2065499225 returns insertion order rather than the source example's displayed order, proving that retrieval lists must be judged order-insensitively.

The protected app source and immutable native source retain SHA-256 values 956036f33b9c786fb1d385c4c3c58dd45a2111f1e4bd528899592f4092489cd8 and b083ee8ac8dbf4b321625c443e0655ac0bb540c893bb77c09517017b8f419d56. Both use the same append-only list, granularity map, prefix truncation, inclusive comparison, and output construction; the app adds only the operation-trace adapter and native-compatible annotation differences.

The unchanged 8-, 24-, and 48-log workloads span 6x, grow stored logs and exact-second retrievals together, and remain legal under the 500-call source limit. The exact protected source passed all fourteen outputs with +0.01 extra growth and a 1.01x largest-tier ratio. An independently correct control that insertion-sorts a fresh reverse-ordered copy before every retrieval passed every output but failed only scaling at +1.63 extra growth and 79.31x.

The refreshed Approach exactly describes append-only storage, fixed prefix lengths, lexicographic and chronological equivalence, inclusive truncated boundaries, unrestricted result order, O(1) put time, O(P) retrieve time, O(QP) trace time, and O(P) stored space.

The authenticated statement contains the log-format description, one three-operation class contract list, exactly one explained example, and exactly eight constraints, with no notes, tables, images, diagrams, follow-up, or hints. The modular Reference preserves the exact example arrays and output, every explanation step, all field and call bounds, and the precision semantics; source_fidelity.json validates without errors.

coverage: The sole authenticated source example appears first with its exact operation array, argument array, and [null,null,null,null,[3,2,1],[2,1]] output. The ordered_results_unordered_lists validator preserves operation-result positions while accepting the protected and verified native [1,2,3]/[1,2] ordering, as required by the source's order-independent return contract.

Visible contract boundaries cover IDs 1 and 500, years 2000 and 2017, months 1 and 12, days 1 and 31, hours 0 and 23, minutes and seconds 0 and 59, all six granularities, and exactly 500 combined put/retrieve calls.

Material semantics cover ignored lower-order fields, complete inclusion of both truncated endpoint buckets, transitions at every timestamp precision, duplicate exact timestamps, hundreds of matches, empty results, nonchronological insertion, persistence across repeated retrievals, and unrestricted result ordering.

An independent oracle parsed timestamps into six-integer tuples rather than reusing string prefixes. It verified both protected forms on all eleven visible cases, all three benchmarks, 468 exhaustive granularity/range queries over twelve boundary-heavy timestamps, and 500 deterministic legal 60-call traces totaling 30,000 operations with seed 63520260804.

All eleven ordinary cases are visible samples or trials. The unchanged 8-, 24-, and 48-log reverse-ordered workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, use 16, 48, and 96 legal API calls, span 6x, and make the correct cubic-trace insertion-sort control fail only scaling.
